opt2: A captain of the temple guard who offered sacrifices at the altar
opt3: A centurion of the Italian band, a devout man who feared God and gave much alms
opt4: A governor of the province of Syria who protected the disciples
correct: A centurion of the Italian band, a devout man who feared God and gave much alms
explanation: Cornelius was a pious Roman centurion renowned for prayer and almsgiving. Acts 10:1-2 (KJV) - "There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band, A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway."

question: What divine assessment did the angel give regarding Cornelius' prayers and alms?
opt1: Thy gifts have purchased pardon for thy Roman ancestors
opt2: Thy piety shall be rewarded with governorship in Judaea
opt3: Thy sacrifices are numbered among the priests of Aaron
opt4: Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God
correct: Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God
explanation: Cornelius' devotional life ascended as a fragrant memorial offering to God. Acts 10:4 (KJV) - "And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God."

question: What vision did Peter behold on the housetop in Joppa when he became very hungry at the sixth hour?
opt1: Heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth
opt2: A ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending
opt3: A golden altar with seven censers burning with incense
opt4: Four living creatures having the faces of a lion, ox, man, and eagle
correct: Heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth
explanation: Peter's trance revealed a great sheet containing all manner of animals descending from heaven. Acts 10:11 (KJV) - "And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:"

question: What divine rule did the heavenly voice give to Peter when he refused to eat animals deemed common or unclean by the Law?
opt1: Eat only the clean beasts according to the ordinance of Moses
opt2: What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common
opt3: Touch not the unclean thing until the evening sacrifice
opt4: The law of foods abideth for ever throughout your generations
correct: What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common
explanation: God abolished ceremonial dietary distinctions to signify the inclusion of Gentiles. Acts 10:15 (KJV) - "And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common."

question: What did Peter do when Cornelius fell down at his feet and worshipped him upon entering his house?
opt1: He laid his hands upon Cornelius' head and blessed his household
opt2: He commanded Cornelius to offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving
opt3: Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man
opt4: He accepted his homage as an apostle of the Lord
correct: Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man
explanation: Peter unequivocally rejected creature worship, affirming his common humanity. Acts 10:26 (KJV) - "But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man."

question: What theological realization did Peter announce as he opened his mouth to preach in Cornelius' house?
opt1: Salvation belongeth exclusively to the circumcision of Israel
opt2: The Gentiles must first be circumcised before receiving the gospel
opt3: Caesar's soldiers shall judge the twelve tribes of Jacob
opt4: Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him
correct: Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him
explanation: Peter recognized that God shows no national or ethnic favoritism in salvation. Acts 10:34-35 (KJV) - "Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him."

question: How did Peter summarize the earthly ministry and divine empowerment of Jesus of Nazareth?
opt1: God anointed Him with the Holy Ghost and power, and He went about doing good and healing
opt2: He was a prophet who restored the kingdom of David by mighty signs
opt3: He preached the destruction of the temple and established new feast days
opt4: He gathered twelve armies to overthrow the Roman legions
correct: God anointed Him with the Holy Ghost and power, and He went about doing good and healing
explanation: Peter delivered this classic summary of Christ's benevolent, Spirit-anointed ministry. Acts 10:38 (KJV) - "How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him."

question: What dramatic spiritual phenomenon occurred while Peter was yet speaking these words to Cornelius' household?
opt1: An earthquake shook the foundations of Cornelius' palace
opt2: The Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word
opt3: An angel appeared and placed golden crowns upon their heads
opt4: The sheet from heaven descended once more before their eyes
correct: The Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word
explanation: The Holy Spirit fell sovereignly upon the Gentile listeners as they heard the gospel. Acts 10:44 (KJV) - "While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word."

question: Why were the believers of the circumcision who came with Peter astonished at Cornelius' house?
opt1: Because Cornelius refused to pay tribute to the temple
opt2: Because Roman soldiers laid down their weapons before Peter
opt3: Because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost
opt4: Because the Gentiles spoke fluent Hebrew and Aramaic
correct: Because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost
explanation: Jewish believers were astonished that Gentiles received the identical gift of the Holy Spirit. Acts 10:45 (KJV) - "And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost."

question: What rhetorical question did Peter ask to justify the immediate water baptism of these Gentile converts?
opt1: Can any man require circumcision before they enter the fold?
opt2: Shall we send messengers to the Sanhedrin for their approval?
opt3: Must they first fast seven days according to our custom?
opt4: Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?
correct: Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?
explanation: Their reception of the Spirit was indisputable proof of their fitness for baptism. Acts 10:47 (KJV) - "Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?"

question: What accusation did they of the circumcision bring against Peter when he came up to Jerusalem after visiting Cornelius?
opt1: Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them
opt2: Thou hast taken silver from a Roman centurion to buy land
opt3: Thou hast broken the vow of the Nazarites in Joppa
opt4: Thou hast preached that the temple in Jerusalem shall be burned
correct: Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them
explanation: They criticized Peter for violating ceremonial table fellowship with uncircumcised Gentiles. Acts 11:3 (KJV) - "Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them."

question: What conclusion did the apostles and brethren in Jerusalem reach after hearing Peter rehearse the entire matter?
opt1: They commanded that Cornelius be circumcised before the next feast
opt2: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life
opt3: They forbade Peter from preaching outside the borders of Judaea
opt4: They resolved to send twelve priests to inspect the house in Caesarea
correct: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life
explanation: The Jerusalem leadership glorified God for extending saving repentance to Gentiles. Acts 11:18 (KJV) - "When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life."

question: Whom did the church in Jerusalem send forth to Antioch when they heard that a great number of Grecians believed and turned unto the Lord?
opt1: Silas
opt2: Matthias
opt3: Barnabas
opt4: John Mark
correct: Barnabas
explanation: Barnabas was dispatched to oversee and encourage the booming revival in Antioch. Acts 11:22 (KJV) - "Then tidings of these things came unto the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch."

question: How is Barnabas' character described when he came to Antioch and saw the grace of God?
opt1: A mighty warrior who defended the church against the heathen
opt2: A strict keeper of the Law who fasted thrice in the week
opt3: A wealthy merchant who gave all his goods to the poor
opt4: A good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith
correct: A good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith
explanation: Barnabas was characterized by goodness, spiritual fullness, and vibrant faith. Acts 11:24 (KJV) - "For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord."

question: Where did Barnabas depart to seek Saul in order to bring him to co-labor in the church at Antioch?
opt1: To Tarsus
opt2: To Jerusalem
opt3: To Damascus
opt4: To Caesarea
correct: To Tarsus
explanation: Barnabas traveled to Tarsus to enlist Saul's teaching gifts for Antioch. Acts 11:25 (KJV) - "Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul:"

question: In which city were the disciples of Jesus called Christians first?
opt1: In Jerusalem
opt2: In Antioch
opt3: In Damascus
opt4: In Rome
correct: In Antioch
explanation: The historic designation 'Christian' originated in Syrian Antioch. Acts 11:26 (KJV) - "And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch."

question: Which prophet came from Jerusalem unto Antioch and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world?
opt1: Judas Barsabas
opt2: Silas
opt3: Agabus
opt4: Manaen
correct: Agabus
explanation: Agabus predicted the empire-wide famine that occurred under Claudius Caesar. Acts 11:28 (KJV) - "And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar."

question: By whose hands did the disciples in Antioch send relief unto the brethren who dwelt in Judaea?
opt1: By Peter and John
opt2: By Stephen and Philip
opt3: By Timothy and Titus
opt4: By the hands of Barnabas and Saul
correct: By the hands of Barnabas and Saul
explanation: Barnabas and Saul carried the relief funds directly to the Jerusalem elders. Acts 11:30 (KJV) - "Which also they did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul."

question: Under which Roman emperor did the empire-wide famine foretold by Agabus take place?
opt1: Claudius Caesar
opt2: Tiberius Caesar
opt3: Nero Caesar
opt4: Caesar Augustus
correct: Claudius Caesar
explanation: Luke anchors the historical fulfillment to the reign of Claudius Caesar. Acts 11:28 (KJV) - "which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar."

question: How did the believers in Antioch determine the amount of relief each disciple should send to Judaea?
opt1: Each man was assessed a fixed tax of two drachmas
opt2: Every man according to his ability
opt3: They cast lots to determine whose fields should be sold
opt4: Only the elders and deacons were permitted to contribute
correct: Every man according to his ability
explanation: Giving was voluntary, proportionate, and based upon individual ability. Acts 11:29 (KJV) - "Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea:"

question: Which apostle was executed by Herod the king with the sword in Acts 12:2?
opt1: Peter the brother of Andrew
opt2: Philip of Bethsaida
opt3: James the brother of John
opt4: Thomas called Didymus
correct: James the brother of John
explanation: James the son of Zebedee was the first of the twelve apostles martyred. Acts 12:2 (KJV) - "And he killed James the brother of John with the sword."

question: During which Jewish feast did Herod arrest Peter, intending to bring him forth to the people after Easter (Passover)?
opt1: The feast of the dedication
opt2: The feast of tabernacles
opt3: The feast of Pentecost
opt4: The Days of Unleavened Bread
correct: The Days of Unleavened Bread
explanation: Peter's arrest occurred during the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Acts 12:3 (KJV) - "And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)"

question: What was the church doing while Peter was kept in prison guarded by four quaternions of soldiers?
opt1: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him
opt2: The believers fled from Jerusalem into the mountains of Samaria
opt3: The church gathered money to pay a ransom unto King Herod
opt4: The elders appealed to the Roman governor in Caesarea
correct: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him
explanation: The church engaged in persistent, unceasing intercession for Peter's deliverance. Acts 12:5 (KJV) - "Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him."

question: How did the angel of the Lord awaken Peter as he slept between two soldiers bound with two chains?
opt1: He blew a trumpet that shook the dungeon
opt2: Smote Peter on the side and raised him up, causing his chains to fall off
opt3: He poured sweet oil upon his brow
opt4: He called him by his new name Cephas three times
correct: Smote Peter on the side and raised him up, causing his chains to fall off
explanation: The angel struck Peter's side to awaken him and miraculously loosed his chains. Acts 12:7 (KJV) - "And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands."

question: What gate of the city opened unto Peter and the angel of its own accord?
opt1: The Beautiful gate of the temple

opt4: The Valley gate leading to the brook Cedron

explanation: The massive iron gate opened autonomously by divine power. Acts 12:10 (KJV) - "When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him."

question: To whose house did Peter come where many were gathered together praying?
opt1: To the house of Nicodemus the ruler

opt4: To the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying
correct: To the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying
explanation: The prayer meeting was hosted at the home of Mary, mother of John Mark. Acts 12:12 (KJV) - "And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying."

question: Who was the damsel that came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate, and failed to open it for gladness?
opt1: A damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda
opt2: A maiden named Tabitha
opt3: A servant named Lydia
opt4: A woman named Joanna
correct: A damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda
explanation: Rhoda recognized Peter's voice and in her joyful excitement ran in without opening the gate. Acts 12:13-14 (KJV) - "And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda. And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate."

question: What did the praying believers insist when Rhoda constantly affirmed that Peter stood at the gate?
opt1: Thou hast seen a phantom of the night
opt2: Thou art mad. Then said they, It is his angel
opt3: The Roman guards have come to arrest us also
opt4: Peter is asleep between two soldiers in the dungeon
correct: Thou art mad. Then said they, It is his angel
explanation: They incredulously dismissed Rhoda's report, guessing it was Peter's guardian angel. Acts 12:15 (KJV) - "And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then said they, It is his angel."

question: What blasphemous acclamation did the people shout when Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, made an oration in Caesarea?
opt1: Behold the king who shall deliver us from Caesar
opt2: Worthy is Herod to sit upon the throne of David
opt3: It is the voice of a god, and not of a man
opt4: The god of Rome hath spoken peace unto Phoenicia
correct: It is the voice of a god, and not of a man
explanation: The crowd flatteringly hailed Herod's voice as that of a god rather than a human. Acts 12:22 (KJV) - "And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man."

question: Why did the angel of the Lord smite Herod, and what was the gruesome manner of his death?
opt1: Because he consulted magicians, and his palace was burned with fire
opt2: Because he allied with Tyre and Sidon, and he was drowned in the sea
opt3: Because he desecrated the sabbath, and he fell from his chariot
opt4: Because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost
correct: Because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost
explanation: Herod was struck down for usurping divine glory and died eaten of worms. Acts 12:23 (KJV) - "And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost."

question: What specific command did the Holy Ghost speak to the church at Antioch as they ministered to the Lord and fasted?
opt1: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them
opt2: Send twelve elders to preach in the synagogues of Rome
opt3: Build a temple of stone in Antioch for the Gentiles
opt4: Cease your fasting and celebrate the feast of the Passover
correct: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them
explanation: The Holy Spirit directly initiated the first organized foreign missionary journey. Acts 13:2 (KJV) - "As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them."

question: Who was Sergius Paulus, and who was the sorcerer that sought to turn him away from the faith in Paphos?
opt1: A Roman centurion; Simon Magus

opt3: The governor of Syria; Alexander the coppersmith
opt4: A chief scribe of Cyprus; Demetrius the silversmith
correct: The deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; and Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation)
explanation: Proconsul Sergius Paulus was opposed by Elymas (Bar-jesus) the false prophet. Acts 13:7-8 (KJV) - "Which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God. But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith."

question: At what point in the narrative of Acts is Saul first referred to by his Roman name 'Paul'?
opt1: When he was ordained by the elders in Jerusalem

opt3: When confronting Elymas the sorcerer before Sergius Paulus
opt4: When he arrived in Athens at the Areopagus
correct: When confronting Elymas the sorcerer before Sergius Paulus
explanation: Luke transitions from Saul to Paul during the confrontation with Elymas on Cyprus. Acts 13:9 (KJV) - "Then Saul, (who also is called Paul,) filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him,"

question: What judgment fell upon Elymas the sorcerer when Paul rebuked him as a child of the devil?
opt1: He was smitten with perpetual leprosy as Gehazi
opt2: He fell down dead as Ananias and Sapphira
opt3: His tongue was silenced so that he could not speak for three years

correct: Thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand
explanation: Elymas was struck with temporary blindness, demonstrating God's judgment over demonic deceit. Acts 13:11 (KJV) - "And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand."

question: What did John Mark do when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia?

opt4: He fell sick of a fever and died at Perga

explanation: John Mark abandoned the mission team at Perga, returning to Jerusalem. Acts 13:13 (KJV) - "Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departing from them returned to Jerusalem."

question: What divine testimony did God bear concerning King David in Paul's synagogue sermon at Antioch in Pisidia?
opt1: David is the wisest among the kings of the earth

opt3: David shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever
opt4: His throne shall never lack a sword to defend Zion
correct: I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will
explanation: Paul quoted 1 Samuel 13:14: David was a man after God's own heart. Acts 13:22 (KJV) - "to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will."

question: How did Paul demonstrate the contrast between King David and Jesus Christ regarding physical corruption?
opt1: David died in battle, but Jesus gave his life voluntarily

opt3: David saw corruption, but He whom God raised saw no corruption
opt4: David's bones were carried into Babylon, but Christ's remained in Judaea

Acts 13:36-37 (KJV) - "For David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep, and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption: But he, whom God raised again, saw no corruption."

question: What magnificent doctrine of justification did Paul preach in the Pisidian Antioch synagogue?
opt1: Circumcision on the eighth day cleanseth all past transgressions

opt3: Obedience to the traditions of the elders granteth eternal righteousness
opt4: By Him all that believe are justified from all things which Moses' law could not justify
correct: By Him all that believe are justified from all things which Moses' law could not justify
explanation: Justification by faith in Christ accomplishes what the Mosaic Law was powerless to effect. Acts 13:39 (KJV) - "And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses."

question: What pivotal declaration did Paul and Barnabas make to the envious Jews who contradicted and blasphemed on the next sabbath?
opt1: It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles

opt3: The Roman governor shall banish your synagogue from the province
opt4: Your temple shall be left desolate within forty days
correct: It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles
explanation: Jewish rejection prompted the decisive turn of the apostolic mission toward the Gentiles. Acts 13:46 (KJV) - "Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles."

question: Who among the Gentiles believed when they heard Paul's declaration of turning unto them?
opt1: All who were trained in the philosophy of the Greeks

opt3: Those who had paid vows in the court of the proselytes
opt4: Those who were enrolled in the Roman census
correct: As many as were ordained to eternal life
explanation: Luke attributes the Gentiles' saving faith to sovereign divine ordination. Acts 13:48 (KJV) - "And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed."

question: In Lystra, what physical ailment did the man have whom Paul perceived had faith to be healed?
opt1: He had a withered right hand from his youth
opt2: He was stricken with blindness for forty years
opt3: A cripple from his mother's womb, who never had walked
opt4: He had an issue of blood for twelve years
correct: A cripple from his mother's womb, who never had walked
explanation: The man had been completely lame from birth and had never walked. Acts 14:8 (KJV) - "And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother's womb, who never had walked:"

question: What did the pagan people of Lystra shout in the speech of Lycaonia when they saw the lame man leap and walk?
opt1: The prophets of the Hebrews have conquered our city
opt2: These are sorcerers sent from the court of Egypt
opt3: The Roman emperors have sent healers unto Lycaonia
opt4: The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men
correct: The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men
explanation: The pagans mistook the apostles for visiting Olympian deities in human form. Acts 14:11 (KJV) - "And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men."

question: What pagan mythological names did the people of Lystra ascribe to Barnabas and Paul?
opt1: Barnabas as Jupiter, and Paul as Mercurius

opt3: They called Barnabas, Saturn; and Paul, Vulcan
opt4: They called Barnabas, Hercules; and Paul, Castor
correct: Barnabas as Jupiter, and Paul as Mercurius
explanation: Barnabas was identified as Jupiter (Zeus) and Paul as Mercurius (Hermes). Acts 14:12 (KJV) - "And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker."

question: How did the priest of Jupiter attempt to honor the apostles before the gates of Lystra?
opt1: Brought twelve golden crowns and robes of purple

opt4: Built two altars of marble in the center of the market
correct: Brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people
explanation: The priest brought sacrificial bulls draped with floral garlands to sacrifice to them. Acts 14:13 (KJV) - "Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people."

question: What did Barnabas and Paul do when they heard that the crowds were preparing to offer sacrifice unto them?
opt1: They accepted their offerings and gave them to the poor
opt2: They called down fire from heaven to consume the oxen
opt3: They rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out, And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you
opt4: They hid themselves in the house of a certain believer
correct: They rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out, And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you
explanation: The apostles tore their clothes in grief, vehemently rejecting divine honors. Acts 14:14-15 (KJV) - "Which when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out, And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you,"

question: What natural witnesses did Paul cite to show that the living God had never left Himself without witness even among Gentile nations?
opt1: The constellations of Orion and the Pleiades in the heavens
opt2: The wisdom of the Greek poets and philosophers
opt3: The laws written on tables of stone given to the fathers
opt4: In that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness
correct: In that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness
explanation: God's common grace in rain, fruitful harvests, and food testifies to His benevolent existence. Acts 14:17 (KJV) - "Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness."

question: What violence did the fickle multitude inflict upon Paul at Lystra after being persuaded by Jews from Antioch and Iconium?
opt1: They stoned Paul and drew him out of the city, supposing him dead
opt2: They beat him with rods and cast him into the dungeon
opt3: They bound him in chains and delivered him to the Roman cohort
opt4: They threw him headlong from the brow of the hill
correct: They stoned Paul and drew him out of the city, supposing him dead
explanation: Paul was stoned and dragged outside the city walls, presumed dead. Acts 14:19 (KJV) - "And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead."

question: What miraculous resilience did Paul display as the disciples stood round about his battered body outside Lystra?
opt1: He was carried upon a stretcher into the house of Lydia
opt2: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe
opt3: An angel lifted him up and transported him to Azotus
opt4: He slept for three days and was healed by fasting
correct: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe
explanation: God revived Paul, who boldly re-entered the very city where he was stoned. Acts 14:20 (KJV) - "Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe."

question: What realistic truth concerning the Christian life did Paul and Barnabas preach while confirming the souls of disciples in Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch?
opt1: That believers shall enjoy immunity from earthly sorrow and poverty
opt2: That all earthly rulers shall soon bow before the church
opt3: That we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God
opt4: That the year of jubilee shall abolish all persecutions
correct: That we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God
explanation: They taught that hardship and tribulation are the appointed pathway to the kingdom. Acts 14:22 (KJV) - "Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God."

question: What ecclesiastical practice did Paul and Barnabas establish in every newly planted church on their return journey?
opt1: They collected a tenth of all grain for the poor in Jerusalem
opt2: They appointed seven deacons to administer table charity
opt3: They built stone synagogues according to the pattern of Galilee
opt4: Ordained elders in every church with prayer and fasting
correct: Ordained elders in every church with prayer and fasting
explanation: Local churches were established under the spiritual oversight of ordained elders. Acts 14:23 (KJV) - "And when they had ordained them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed."

question: What legalistic doctrine did certain men who came down from Judaea teach the brethren at Antioch?
opt1: Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved
opt2: Except ye pay tithes of all herbs, ye shall not inherit the kingdom
opt3: Except ye worship only in the temple at Jerusalem, your prayers are vain
opt4: Except ye keep the traditions of the elders, ye cannot break bread
correct: Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved
explanation: Judaizers insisted that Mosaic circumcision was mandatory for salvation. Acts 15:1 (KJV) - "And certain men which came down from Judaea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved."

question: How did the Apostle Peter explain the salvation of Gentiles during the council at Jerusalem?
opt1: By their strict compliance with the dietary laws of Moses
opt2: God put no difference between Jews and Gentiles, purifying their hearts by faith
opt3: Through their offerings brought unto the elders of Zion
opt4: By their circumcision on the eighth day after baptism
correct: God put no difference between Jews and Gentiles, purifying their hearts by faith
explanation: God purifies human hearts through faith without ethnic distinction. Acts 15:9 (KJV) - "And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith."

question: What profound truth of universal grace did Peter articulate in Acts 15:11?
opt1: Circumcision is the seal of righteousness for all nations
opt2: The Law of Moses is an easy yoke for all believers
opt3: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they
opt4: The kingdom of God is inherited by works of righteousness
correct: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they
explanation: Both Jews and Gentiles are saved exclusively through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ. Acts 15:11 (KJV) - "But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they."

question: Which Old Testament prophecy from Amos did James quote to support the inclusion of the Gentiles?
opt1: The mountain of the Lord's house shall be established in the top of the mountains
opt2: I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh
opt3: A star shall rise out of Jacob and smite the corners of Moab
opt4: I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down
correct: I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down
explanation: James cited Amos to show God's eternal plan to rebuild David's fallen tent among the Gentiles. Acts 15:16-17 (KJV) - "After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things."

question: What four prohibitions did the Jerusalem Council write unto Gentile believers to observe for fellowship?
opt1: That they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood
opt2: To keep the sabbath, fast twice a week, tithe their herbs, and wear phylacteries
opt3: To avoid military service, refuse Roman coins, swear no oaths, and avoid meat
opt4: To shave their heads, offer turtle doves, wash before meals, and observe new moons
correct: That they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood
explanation: The council urged abstinence from idolatry, sexual immorality, strangled meat, and blood. Acts 15:20 (KJV) - "But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood."

question: Which two leading prophets from Jerusalem were sent to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas to deliver the council's decree?
opt1: Timothy and Titus
opt2: Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas
opt3: Prochorus and Nicanor
opt4: Agabus and Philip
correct: Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas
explanation: Judas Barsabas and Silas confirmed the letter's authenticity verbally. Acts 15:22 (KJV) - "Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:"

question: What disagreement caused a sharp contention between Paul and Barnabas prior to their proposed second missionary journey?
opt1: Whether to receive tithes from the Gentile congregations
opt2: Whether to preach in the cities of Galatia or Macedonia
opt3: Whether to take John Mark with them
opt4: Whether Silas should be ordained an apostle
correct: Whether to take John Mark with them
explanation: They clashed over John Mark, who had previously deserted them in Pamphylia. Acts 15:37-39 (KJV) - "And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work. And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;"

question: Whom did Paul choose as his missionary companion when he departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God?
opt1: Timothy
opt2: Titus
opt3: Luke
opt4: Silas
correct: Silas
explanation: Paul selected Silas (Silvanus) for his second missionary expedition. Acts 15:40 (KJV) - "And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God."

question: Through which provinces did Paul and Silas travel as they began the second missionary journey, confirming the churches?
opt1: Through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches
opt2: Through Egypt and Cyrene
opt3: Through Pontus and Bithynia
opt4: Through the islands of Cyprus and Crete
correct: Through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches
explanation: Paul strengthened established congregations in Syria and Cilicia. Acts 15:41 (KJV) - "And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches."

question: Why did Paul refuse to take John Mark on the second journey?
opt1: Because Mark was not of the seed of Abraham
opt2: He had departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work
opt3: Because Mark had fallen sick of a fever in Antioch
opt4: Because Mark had not been ordained by the twelve in Jerusalem
correct: He had departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work
explanation: Paul considered Mark unreliable due to his abandonment in Pamphylia. Acts 15:38 (KJV) - "But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work."

question: What was the mixed heritage of the young disciple Timotheus whom Paul met at Derbe and Lystra?
opt1: His father was a Roman centurion and his mother was an Egyptian
opt2: Both his parents were proselytes of the Antioch church
opt3: The son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek
opt4: His father was a Levite and his mother was a Samaritan
correct: The son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek
explanation: Timothy had a devout Jewish-Christian mother (Eunice) and a Gentile Greek father. Acts 16:1 (KJV) - "Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:"

question: Why did Paul circumcise Timothy prior to taking him along on his missionary journeys?
opt1: Because the Jerusalem decree required it for all ministers
opt2: To earn favor with the high priest in Jerusalem
opt3: Because Timothy could not enter synagogues without circumcision
opt4: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek
correct: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek
explanation: Paul circumcised Timothy for missional expediency and access to Jewish audiences. Acts 16:3 (KJV) - "Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek."

question: How did the Holy Spirit direct the itinerary of Paul and his companions when they attempted to preach in Asia and Bithynia?
opt1: They were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia
opt2: An angel told them to build a tabernacle in Galatia
opt3: A great storm destroyed their ship at sea
opt4: The Roman governor arrested them at the border
correct: They were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia
explanation: The Spirit sovereignly restrained them from Asia and Bithynia to guide them to Europe. Acts 16:6 (KJV) - "Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,"

question: What vision appeared to Paul in the night at Troas that summoned him to evangelize Europe?
opt1: An angel holding a burning torch above Rome
opt2: There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us
opt3: A great white sheet filled with books descending from heaven
opt4: The apostle Peter beckoning him from Antioch
correct: There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us
explanation: The 'Macedonian Call' directed the gospel across the Aegean Sea into Europe. Acts 16:9 (KJV) - "And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us."

question: Who was Lydia of Thyatira, the first recorded European convert in Philippi?
opt1: A priestess in the temple of Diana at Ephesus
opt2: A handmaid in the palace of the Roman praetor
opt3: A seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God... whose heart the Lord opened
opt4: The wife of the Philippian jailor
correct: A seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God... whose heart the Lord opened
explanation: Lydia was a prosperous merchant of purple goods whose heart God opened to the gospel. Acts 16:14 (KJV) - "And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul."

question: What spirit possessed the damsel in Philippi who followed Paul crying, 'These men are the servants of the most high God'?
opt1: A spirit of muteness and deafness
opt2: A spirit of lunacy and epilepsy
opt3: A spirit of uncleanness and leprosy
opt4: A certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination... which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying
correct: A certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination... which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying
explanation: She was controlled by a Python spirit (spirit of divination) exploited for profit. Acts 16:16 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:"

question: What were Paul and Silas doing at midnight in the inner prison of Philippi, with their feet made fast in the stocks?
opt1: Prayed, and sang praises unto God
opt2: They mourned and wept for their companions
opt3: They wrote letters of appeal unto the Roman senate
opt4: They fasted and slept upon the cold stone floor
correct: Prayed, and sang praises unto God
explanation: Despite painful wounds and stocks, they prayed and sang praises to God at midnight. Acts 16:25 (KJV) - "And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them."

question: What was the jailor about to do when an earthquake opened all the prison doors and loosed everyone's bands?
opt1: He fled unto the house of the magistrates for safety
opt2: He drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled
opt3: He summoned fifty soldiers with spears to execute the prisoners
opt4: He fell into a deep trance of terror
correct: He drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled
explanation: Roman law punished jailors with death if prisoners escaped, leading him to attempt suicide. Acts 16:27 (KJV) - "And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled."

question: What is the classic, straightforward answer Paul and Silas gave when the trembling jailor asked, 'Sirs, what must I do to be saved?'
opt1: Offer your service to the temple and fast forty days
opt2: Wash your hands and obey the ten commandments of Moses
opt3: Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house
opt4: Give half your goods to the poor and swear no oaths
correct: Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house
explanation: Acts 16:31 states the essential gospel response: saving faith in Jesus Christ. Acts 16:31 (KJV) - "And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house."

question: Why did Paul refuse to depart secretly from Philippi when the magistrates sent serjeants saying, 'Let those men go'?
opt1: Because they had not yet collected their traveling provisions
opt2: Because the believers in Lydia's house had not finished praying
opt3: Because they were waiting for the arrival of Timothy and Silas
opt4: They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out
correct: They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out
explanation: Paul asserted his Roman citizenship rights, demanding public vindication from the magistrates. Acts 16:37 (KJV) - "But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out."

question: For how many sabbath days did Paul reason with the Jews out of the scriptures in the synagogue of Thessalonica?
opt1: Three sabbath days
opt2: For seven sabbath days
opt3: For forty days continually
opt4: For twelve sabbaths
correct: Three sabbath days
explanation: Paul spent three consecutive sabbaths demonstrating Christ from Old Testament scriptures. Acts 17:2 (KJV) - "And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,"

question: What famous charge did the envious mob bring against Jason and the brethren before the rulers of Thessalonica?
opt1: These men are magicians from Egypt who lead the poor astray
opt2: These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also
opt3: These have robbed the treasury of Caesar in Macedonia
opt4: These have broken the peace of the Olympic games
correct: These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also
explanation: The gospel's radical cultural impact was described as turning the world upside down. Acts 17:6 (KJV) - "And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;"

question: Why were the believers in Berea commended as 'more noble than those in Thessalonica'?
opt1: Because they were descendants of the royal house of Macedon
opt2: Because they gave large amounts of gold to the apostles
opt3: In that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so
opt4: Because they built three synagogues for the disciples
correct: In that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so
explanation: The Bereans verified all apostolic preaching daily against the written Scriptures. Acts 17:11 (KJV) - "These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so."

question: What deeply stirred Paul's spirit when he walked through the historic city of Athens waiting for Silas and Timothy?
opt1: The magnificent architecture of the Parthenon
opt2: The dialectic debates of the philosophers in the market
opt3: The vast numbers of Roman soldiers garrisoned in Greece
opt4: His spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry
correct: His spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry
explanation: Paul was deeply grieved by the pervasive idol worship throughout Athens. Acts 17:16 (KJV) - "Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry."

question: Which two philosophical schools in Athens encountered Paul and debated with him in the Agora?
opt1: The Epicureans and the Stoics
opt2: The Platonists and the Aristotelians
opt3: The Cynics and the Pythagoreans
opt4: The Sophists and the Gnostics
correct: The Epicureans and the Stoics
explanation: Paul engaged the two leading Hellenistic philosophical schools: Epicureans and Stoics. Acts 17:18 (KJV) - "Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection."

question: To what historic judicial hill in Athens did the philosophers bring Paul to explain his new doctrine?
opt1: The Acropolis
opt2: Areopagus (Mars' Hill)
opt3: The Pnyx
opt4: Mount Lycabettus

explanation: Paul addressed the intellectual elite on Mars' Hill (the Areopagus). Acts 17:19 (KJV) - "And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?"

question: What specific altar inscription did Paul use as the starting point for his sermon on Mars' Hill?
opt1: TO THE KING OF HEAVEN
opt2: TO THE GOD OF PEACE
opt3: TO THE UNKNOWN GOD
opt4: TO THE FATHER OF ALL GODS
correct: TO THE UNKNOWN GOD
explanation: Paul used their altar dedicated 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD' to proclaim the true Creator. Acts 17:23 (KJV) - "For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you."

question: What Greek poetic quotation regarding man's total dependence on God did Paul cite to the Athenians?
opt1: All men are mortal and pass away as grass

opt3: Wisdom is the highest good of mortal existence
opt4: In Him we live, and move, and have our being; for we are also His offspring
correct: In Him we live, and move, and have our being; for we are also His offspring
explanation: Paul quoted Cilician poet Aratus to establish divine immanence and human dependence. Acts 17:28 (KJV) - "For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring."

question: What universal moral command does God now issue unto all men everywhere, seeing the times of ignorance have passed?
opt1: God now commandeth all men every where to repent

opt3: To study the philosophy of the Hebrews
opt4: To build temples of white marble in every city
correct: God now commandeth all men every where to repent
explanation: With the coming of Christ, God commands universal repentance. Acts 17:30 (KJV) - "And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:"

question: What guarantee did God provide that He will judge the world in righteousness by that Man whom He hath ordained?
opt1: He inscribed the moral law upon the stones of Sinai
opt2: Whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead
opt3: He sent the prophets to record the vision of judgment
opt4: He caused the sun to stand still in the valley of Ajalon
correct: Whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead
explanation: Christ's resurrection is God's conclusive proof of future universal judgment. Acts 17:31 (KJV) - "Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead."

question: Why had Aquila and his wife Priscilla recently departed from Italy to settle in Corinth?
opt1: Because a famine had broken out throughout the Roman empire

question: What trade or occupation did Paul share with Aquila and Priscilla, which allowed him to support his ministry?
opt1: Fishermen casting nets

explanation: Paul was a skilled tentmaker (leatherworker) by trade. Acts 18:3 (KJV) - "And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers."

question: What symbolic act did Paul perform when the Jews in Corinth opposed themselves and blasphemed?

opt4: He broke an earthen vessel before their eyes

explanation: Paul shook out his garments in prophetic testimony, turning directly to the Gentiles. Acts 18:6 (KJV) - "And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles."

question: Who was Crispus, who believed on the Lord with all his house in Corinth?
opt1: A Roman centurion commanding the local garrison

opt4: The deputy of the province of Achaia

explanation: Crispus, the chief ruler of the Corinthian synagogue, converted with his entire household. Acts 18:8 (KJV) - "And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized."

question: What encouraging vision did the Lord speak to Paul by night in Corinth?
opt1: Arise and depart unto the province of Macedonia without delay
opt2: Gird on thy sword, for the adversary shall surround thy dwelling
opt3: Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city
opt4: Twelve legions of angels shall fight for the believers in Corinth

explanation: Christ promised divine protection and affirmed He had 'much people' in Corinth. question: How long did Paul continue teaching the word of God among the Corinthians during his first stay?
opt1: Six months
opt2: Three years
opt3: Forty days
opt4: A year and six months (18 months)
correct: A year and six months (18 months)
explanation: Paul ministered in Corinth for eighteen months (a year and six months). Acts 18:11 (KJV) - "And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them."

question: Who was the proconsul (deputy) of Achaia who dismissed the Jewish charges against Paul as a matter of internal Jewish law?
opt1: Gallio
opt2: Sergius Paulus
opt3: Pontius Pilate
opt4: Felix the governor
correct: Gallio
explanation: Lucius Junius Gallio dismissed the charges as religious disputes outside Roman jurisdiction. Acts 18:12 (KJV) - "And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,"

question: In which port city did Paul have his head shorn because he had taken a vow?
opt1: In Piraeus
opt2: In Cenchrea
opt3: In Miletus
opt4: In Troas
correct: In Cenchrea
explanation: Paul fulfilled a temporary Nazarite vow by shearing his hair in Cenchrea. Acts 18:18 (KJV) - "And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow."

question: Who was Apollos, and what was the limitation of his knowledge when he arrived in Ephesus?
opt1: A scribe of Antioch who knew only the decrees of the council
opt2: A prophet from Jerusalem who knew only the visions of Agabus
opt3: Apollos of Alexandria, mighty in scriptures but knowing only the baptism of John
opt4: A disciple of Damascus who knew only the law of Moses
correct: Apollos of Alexandria, mighty in scriptures but knowing only the baptism of John
explanation: Apollos was a gifted Alexandrian orator whose theological knowledge ended with John the Baptist. Acts 18:24-25 (KJV) - "And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus. question: Who took Apollos aside and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly?
opt1: Peter and John
